body.statement: Open-ended Question 1. Can the rational-chart handle \(\mathfrak A_{\mathcal I}\) be constructed so that, for every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\) and every \(F_{D,y}\notin K_{\mathcal I}\), some retained chart has a nonzero pullback of \(F_{D,y}\) on a rational open box realizing the exact oracle, with a chart count and grid denominator bounded by \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\); and can the bound be reduced to singly exponential when every minimum DAG has bounded treewidth?
body.justification: This exposes the constructive graph-native content required to prove Theorem 1 without appealing to an unjustified density of rational points on arbitrary CI varieties.
body.gap: Directed-forest CI ideals have tractable prime parameterizations, but no existing atlas is known to be effect-separating for all signatures induced by tied sparsest DAGs.
body.consumer: A positive answer yields finite rational witness search and practical certificate bounds; a negative answer identifies the precise family on which SparseSIM-ID must return algebraic rather than rational witnesses.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct an effect-separating finite rational atlas for every accepted exact oracle and prove both the advertised global height bound and the bounded-treewidth singly exponential refinement.
obligation.obstruction: No frozen hypothesis makes all relevant conditional-independence components rational or proves that DAG and directed-forest charts meet every component detected by an intervention signature.  Bounded treewidth controls graph decompositions but, by itself, does not control rational parametrizability or arithmetic height.
obligation.attempted: Clearing denominators on a single rational chart and searching a Cartesian rational grid works, and the four-node instance supplies one explicit rational curve.  Extending this chartwise argument fails exactly at the unproved coverage or effect-separation step.
obligation.partial_result: One computable conditional result holds.  Let \(\phi:U\to\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) be a rational map defined over \(\mathbb Q\) on a nonempty open box \(U=\prod_{j=1}^k(a_j,b_j)\) with rational endpoints, and suppose all denominators of \(\phi\) are nonzero on \(U\).  If \(F_{D,y}\circ\phi=N/Q\) in reduced form with \(N\in\mathbb Q[t_1,\ldots,t_k]\) nonzero and total degree \(e\), choose \(e+1\) distinct rational numbers in each interval \((a_j,b_j)\).  A nonzero polynomial of degree at most \(e\) cannot vanish on the entire Cartesian grid: induction on \(k\), using the univariate root bound for the last coordinate, proves this assertion.  Thus at most \((e+1)^k\) grid evaluations produce a rational \(t\in U\) with \(N(t)\neq0\), and \(p^\dagger=\phi(t)\) is a strictly positive rational exact-oracle separator.  What remains unproved is that the recursively oriented DAG or forest charts cover every nonzero intervention signature, any uniform comparison of the resulting grid heights with \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\), and any singly exponential bound from bounded treewidth.
